audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Lillia/Skill/Gragas/Gragas/Lillia/Gragas/Gragas while the packet and the already-published mirror both read Skill/Gragas/Skill/Lillia/Gragas/Gragas/Lillia.
audit.why: The content why-strings already argue the packet chart on all seven rows — whys[2] opens 'You're even here', whys[3] is a clean Lillia stage, whys[6] says he never reclaims it. The enum rows were simply stale, and the mirror has already shipped the corrected chart on the Gragas page, so leaving this creates a direct contradiction.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill/Gragas/Skill/Lillia/Gragas/Gragas/Lillia in both layers with ratings moved to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: No spike or phase carries a real cooldown, and the level 6 spike is attributed to a fabricated ability.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 — 14s at rank 1, and it is his engage AND his escape, so the whole cooldown is a window. Explosive Cask is 100s at rank 1. Barrel Roll is 850 range on 10s at rank 1. Lilting Lullaby is 150s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: 14s Body Slam and 100s Explosive Cask written into the phases, spikes, mid and the interactions block.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and mid call Gragas's ultimate 'Body of Burning Cinder'. No such ability exists in his kit.
audit.why: His R is Explosive Cask — 1000 range, 100/85/70, hurls a cask that damages and knocks back. Shipping an invented ability name to a paying user is the exact failure the calibration list warns about.
audit.corrected: Explosive Cask named, with its 100s rank-1 cooldown and the knockback described correctly as anti-chase.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings describe a Gragas 'Q pool' and 'pool sustain'.
audit.why: Barrel Roll is a rolling cask that detonates on command or after 4 seconds and slows — it is not a pool and it does not heal him. His sustain is Happy Hour, which heals him periodically on skill use. Building anti-heal timing around a non-existent pool is bad advice; the real target is a per-cast heal.
audit.corrected: Barrel Roll and Happy Hour named for what they actually do, everywhere the pool appeared.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page states the precondition on Lilting Lullaby.
audit.why: Riot's text: it Drowsies 'all enemies with Dream Dust on them' — no prior Q or E, no sleep at all. The forced wake-up also carries bonus damage, which is why the sleep is a burst setup and not just a stall. The mirror recorded this as the single biggest gap on the Gragas side.
audit.corrected: Precondition and the wake-up bonus written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] calls Body Slam 'his E poke'.
audit.why: Body Slam is a 600-range charge that stuns; the poke is the 850-range Barrel Roll. Conflating them tells the player to respect the wrong range.
audit.corrected: Poke attributed to Barrel Roll at 850, Body Slam to its 600-range stun charge.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet defect: the page never named any of Gragas's abilities.
audit.why: Generic 'his E', 'his Q pool', 'W damage reduction' is the vagueness the rewrite bar exists to remove.
audit.corrected: Happy Hour, Barrel Roll, Drunken Rage, Body Slam and Explosive Cask all named at their real slots.

audit.whatIsWrong: Swirlseed's terrain flag is a tooltip-parsing artefact.
audit.why: Riot's text says the seed rolls until it hits a wall or target; it creates nothing.

edits.before: Level 1 you are weak — one ability, no kite chain — so just farm with the edge of your Q and don't walk into his E body-slam range. Gragas owns the level 2-3 window if he can land E into his Q pool: that dash plus slow is the only way he catches you, and it chunks before your move speed stacks. Respect it, dodge the E, and once you have rank 2-3 Q plus the E slow you start the Dream Dust burn and the lane flips — he has to walk at you and every step costs him HP.
edits.after: Level 1 you are weak — one ability, no kite chain — so farm with the edge of your Q and stay outside Body Slam's 600 units. Gragas owns level 2-3 if he lands Body Slam into Barrel Roll: the charge stuns, the cask slows, and it chunks you before your move speed stacks. Body Slam is 14 seconds at rank 1 — dodge it and the window is yours. Once you have rank 2-3 Q plus the Swirlseed slow the burn starts and he has to walk at you, every step costing HP.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your takeover: full Q rank, the burn DoT compounding, and your sweetspot move speed keep you permanently outside his E range while you grind his pool sustain to nothing. He gets a real spike at 6 — Body of Burning Cinder R can knock you out of a chase or set a gank, so don't tunnel into a kite when his ult is up and a jungler is missing. Bait the E, punish the cooldown, and use your own R to sleep-isolate him if he over-commits.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your takeover: full Q rank, the burn compounding, and stacking move speed keep you outside Body Slam's 600 units while Happy Hour's per-cast heal loses to the DoT. He spikes at 6 — Explosive Cask, 100 seconds at rank 1, knocks you out of a chase or sets a gank, so don't tunnel a kite while his ult is up and a jungler is missing. Body Slam is 14s at rank 1: bait it, then commit. Your R only sleeps targets already carrying Dream Dust, so land Q or E first.
